guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: booking rate wanted, repeat days, diagnostic fee, hours in a technician day and the costs of a technician and a van.
Check Technicians, Vans, Job Types, Call Types, Call Outcomes and Lead Sources. They hold your people, vans and the lists the other sheets look up.
Log every call on Calls with its source, call type, outcome and who answered. The booked flag, the lost value and the act-first score fill in by themselves.
Enter each job on Jobs with the technician, van, hours, price, status and whether parts are confirmed. The days since the last job at the site and the possible-callback flag calculate themselves.
Open Dispatch Board to see each technician and day: jobs, booked and drive hours, free hours and the day check. Open Capacity by Day for the next 30 days.
Write each permit on Permit Log with its dates. Days waiting, days held past the job date and the van cost waiting fill in. Permit Wait shows your own average by job type.
Type the job numbers of the coming days on Work Orders. The date, window, site reference, parts and permit status and the phones for the texts fill in.
Fill Booking by Source, Booking by Answerer, Missed Calls by Weekday and Calls by Month from your call log each month. The booking rates calculate themselves.
Use the 18 tools: each answers one question with a verdict. Change the yellow inputs to try another source, week, job or permit.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Calls and Dispatch Dashboard and the Charts every week. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Contractor Excel Template: Call Log, Dispatch Board, Work Orders, Permit Tracker, Booking Rate, Capacity
listing.headline: From the first call to the closed job: calls, dispatch, work orders and permits
listing.description:
Run the front half of an HVAC and plumbing contractor business in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-run residential and light-commercial service shop with 1 to 15 technicians, an office manager who also dispatches, and a van for each lead technician. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets; a shop with a dispatcher uses the dispatcher columns.

The Calls sheet logs every call with its source, call type, outcome and who answered, and works out the booked flag, the estimated value of unbooked calls and the order in which to call people back. Booking by Source, Booking by Answerer, Missed Calls by Weekday and Calls by Month show your booking rate against the target you set. Jobs holds every job with technician, van, hours, price, status and parts. A second job at the same site inside your repeat window is flagged as a possible callback. The Dispatch Board and Capacity by Day show booked and drive hours, free hours and over-capacity days for each technician.

The Permit Log tracks applied, approved, inspection booked and passed with days waiting and the cost of a van held past its job date. 18 tools answer weekly questions with a clear verdict: booking rate by source, the missed call ranker, the dispatch board, a capacity check for a new job, a same-day slotter, the permit tracker, van waiting cost, a call volume forecast and a jobs-a-week break-even solver. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents such as the work order with a signature line, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to customers, landlord accounts, technicians, the office, your equipment supplier and the accountant.

This is part one of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no per-technician fee: you keep your data. A demo copy full of sample data and a blank copy are included. It helps you keep track of your business and does not promise results.

The diagnostic fee, a fee for coming out to find the cause, is {set:diag_fee}. It is credited if you go ahead with the work. Check the current price before you quote it.
After-hours terms and the price of the work are told before the visit starts. Prices are before sales tax.
The customer confirms the fee below.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business and check your local rules.

documents.title: Callback record with the original job and its cost
paragraphs: Callback record of {set:company}, dated {today}. Job {col:repeats.job_id} on {col:repeats.date}, site reference {col:repeats.site_ref}, {col:repeats.job_type}. Technician: {col:repeats.technician}.

The earlier job at the site was {col:repeats.prev_job} on {col:repeats.prev_date}, {col:repeats.days_between} days before. Technician of the earlier job: {col:repeats.prev_technician}. Flag: {col:repeats.flag}.
Cost of this visit: {col:repeats.cost}. Price of the earlier job: {col:repeats.prev_price}. Cost against the earlier price: {col:repeats.cost_share}.
The reason for the second visit and who follows up are written below.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business and check your local rules.

documents.title: Call log summary for one month
paragraphs: Call log summary of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month starting {col:calls_month.month}.
Calls: {col:calls_month.calls}. Booked: {col:calls_month.booked}. Booking rate: {col:calls_month.booking_rate}. Emergency calls: {col:calls_month.emergency_calls}.
Estimated value of unbooked calls: {col:calls_month.lost_value}. Jobs: {col:calls_month.jobs}. Possible callbacks: {col:calls_month.possible_callbacks}.
Actions for the next review are written below.
